slug: 2026-02-27 Who Protects Nigeria's Digital Citizens Unmasking Accountability Gaps in Digital Rights Governance

facts.fact: Dataphyte describes the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act 2015 as an enacted law whose Section 24 prescribes up to three years' imprisonment or a fine for sending a message known to be false, and says it has been amended.

Reporters Without Borders reported in 2024, as cited by Dataphyte, that at least eight journalists had been arrested, prosecuted or detained under the Cybercrimes Act despite its amendment; no count of cases for a stated period is given.
In December 2024 Lagos nurse Olamide Thomas was arrested after livestreaming remarks critical of the President, charged with cyberbullying and held until bail days later; the document gives no day.

In May 2020 Department of State Services operatives arrested Ambrose Nwaogwugwu, a party social media manager in Imo State, over a satirical post about the governor, charging him with cyber-related offences including defamation and false publication; he was detained several weeks before bail.
